recall.why_it_matters: Measures missed required coverage. Low recall can leave changed payroll or security behavior untested.

precision.why_it_matters: Measures useful recommendations. Low precision consumes consultant time on unnecessary tests.

false_negatives.formula: Count of required golden selections that were not returned
false_negatives.why_it_matters: Review these first. Each case shows the missed test and whether retrieval or later selection failed.

false_positives.formula: Count of returned selections outside the accepted golden answer
false_positives.why_it_matters: Shows wasted regression effort. A wrong test on a positive case produces both an FP and an FN.

exact_match_rate.formula: Cases whose complete selected set equals any accepted golden set / evaluated cases
exact_match_rate.why_it_matters: Measures full set agreement. Empty matches count, so also inspect positive-case accuracy and the decision confusion matrix.

top_k_retrieval_recall.formula: Average fraction of an accepted required set present in the actual K-item shortlist, across gold-match cases
top_k_retrieval_recall.why_it_matters: Separates retrieval problems from LLM problems. The LLM cannot choose a correct test that it never sees.

no_match_accuracy.formula: Correct no_matching_e2e decisions / gold no_matching_e2e cases
no_match_accuracy.why_it_matters: Checks catalog-gap recognition. unable_to_identify is a different decision and receives no credit here.

hallucination_rate.formula: Successful raw responses naming an out-of-catalog test / successful raw responses
hallucination_rate.why_it_matters: Measures invention before guardrails remove invalid names. A valid catalog test outside the shortlist is a retrieval/selection violation, not a catalog hallucination.

confidence_calibration.formula: ECE = sum(bin_count/N * abs(mean_confidence - accuracy)); Brier = mean((confidence - correctness)^2)
confidence_calibration.why_it_matters: Checks whether reported certainty matches observed correctness. Both scores are better near zero. The app score is a heuristic, not a calibrated probability.
